correctness.rationale: On the group basis, a⋆b=Tα(a)Tβ(b) with both factors ordinary ring endomorphisms, including singular β. If an idempotent has augmentation zero then u∈J and u=Tα(u)Tβ(u) repeatedly doubles the ideal power containing it. The presentation K[s₁,…,s_d]/(s₁ᵖ,…,s_dᵖ) with s_i=[e_i]−1 shows nilpotence of J; hence u=0. Otherwise augmentation is one and u is an ordinary unit. Multiplying the idempotency equation out shows L_u M_u=M_u Tβ and R_u M_u=M_u Tα on the entire space, so these are simultaneous similarities and the operators commute. The images of Tβʲ have bases indexed by βʲV, and the stabilized span at step d supports the invertible permutation part. This proves the rank and zero-block formulas by second differences. The fixed-point counts p^dim ker(γˢ−I) give the periodic cycle counts by Möbius inversion. A permutation cycle is cyclic as a K[z]-module with annihilator z^ℓ−1; splitting it for ℓ=pʰe gives precisely the claimed Jordan blocks, also in the wild case. Independently checked the example count: writing u=Σ f_j(S)Tʲ in the F₃ group algebra for the transvection, augmentation one ensures some f_i(1)≠0. The idempotency equation at that i forces Σ f_j(1)S^(−j)=S^(−i), so only f_i has augmentation one. It has 9 choices, and for j≠i the condition (1−S^(j−i))f_j=0 gives 3 choices per f_j in the line spanned by (S−1)². Hence 3·9·3²=243. The rank sequence and cycle lengths in that example also agree.

value.rationale: The common change of basis removes all dependence on the idempotent at once and gives a computable normal form for the pair. This is useful precisely in modular parameters where a Peirce eigenvalue list loses information or one side is singular: both the nonsemisimple cyclic blocks and the nilpotent blocks are accounted for without enumerating idempotents. The result links an established Peirce problem to explicit data for a natural broad class of quandles, not an isolated small example.
residual_risks: The statement does not classify the idempotents themselves or settle analogous Peirce behavior outside the stated modular Alexander setting.
